subject: Post-call: Enterpriseco integration - API auth & key management
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex@enterpriseco.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@enterpriseco.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Enterpriseco integration - API auth & key management

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through Enterpriseco's ingestion and compliance constraints. Per our call, summary + proposed next steps below. Please confirm and add anything I missed.

Key takeaways
- You’ll be evaluating both the hosted Redwood API and a private VPC deployment for higher-control workloads.
- Main concerns: long-lived API keys, auditability (rotation + logs), service account model for machine-to-machine calls, and least-privilege routing for internal teams.
- Primary flows: 1) app server -> Redwood API (inference + embeddings/rerank), 2) background job ingestion -> embeddings, 3) admin console/service -> management APIs.

Recommended short-term approach (POC)
- Use service accounts + short-lived JWTs for server-to-server traffic (avoid long-lived API keys for production).
- For quick evals/early dev: scoped API keys (dev-only) with strict quotas and IP allowlist.
- Enable KV/prefix caching for embeddings workloads we discussed to control costs.

Deliverables attached
- redwood-sdk-setup-guide.pdf (SDK init + examples for OAuth/JWT, API key fallback)
- reqs-key-rotation.xlsx (template for rotation cadence + approval owners)

Next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra team (30-45m) — propose Wed 6/21 10:00am PT or Thu 6/22 2:00pm PT.
2) Dev handoff: we'll create a sandbox service account + sample tokens for you to try.
3) Confirm audit/logging needs (retention window, SIEM export).

Dev, looping you in to own the POC setup and coordinate the deep-dive.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com

On Tue, Jun 20, 2028 at 9:15 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Hi Alex / Priya —
> 
> Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through Enterpriseco's ingestion and compliance constraints. Per our call, summary + proposed next steps below. Please confirm and add anything I missed.

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and captures the call. A few clarifications from our side:
- We prefer service accounts backed by short-lived JWTs if Redwood supports KMS integration for signing keys. Our security team requires that private keys never be exported and rotation be automated.
- For some lower-risk background jobs we can use scoped API keys initially, but want a clear migration path to short-lived creds.
- Audit/logging: 13 months retention, with S3 export and CloudWatch forwarding.

Wed 6/21 10:00am PT works for a technical deep-dive — we'll invite our infra lead (Priya) and one security engineer.

A couple questions for the POC:
1) Does Redwood support OIDC tokens / workload identity federation so we can mint tokens from our OIDC provider?
2) Any recommended rotation cadence for service-account signing keys (we were thinking 30 days)?

Appreciate the attachments — will review and confirm.

— Alex
Alex Turner
Senior Engineering Manager | Enterpriseco
alex@enterpriseco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex@enterpriseco.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Enterpriseco integration - API auth & key management

On Tue, Jun 20, 2028 at 11:04 AM Alex Turner <alex@enterpriseco.com> wrote:
> Thanks Marissa — this looks great and captures the call. A few clarifications from our side: ...

Thanks Alex — quick answers inline and a recommended architecture for the POC below.

Short answers
- KMS/HSM: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS for signing service-account keys; hosted can integrate with KMS providers (AWS KMS / Google KMS) for signing via HSM-backed keys without exporting private material.
- OIDC/WIF: We support OIDC workload identity federation for short-lived tokens (you can mint JWTs via your IdP and exchange for Redwood tokens).
- Rotation cadence: 30 days is reasonable; we recommend automated rotation with overlap (new keys rolled and validated before old keys retire).

Recommended POC auth flow (server-to-server)
1) Create a Redwood service account (scoped to model + embeddings only).
2) Configure your IdP (or Redwood-managed KMS) to sign short-lived JWTs (5-15m TTL) for token exchange.
3) Exchange JWT for Redwood access token via our /v1/auth/exchange endpoint.
4) Use the access token for inference and embeddings calls.
5) Set audit logs to S3 + CloudWatch as you requested; we'll provide sample ingestion config.

Dev notes (for the POC)
- SDKs: our SDKs (Python/Node/Go) provide helpers to do JWT exchange + automatic refresh. Example flow in the attached redwood-sdk-setup-guide.pdf.
- Fallback: scoped API keys for dev with IP allowlist + strict quotas.
- Rotation: we'll provide reqs-key-rotation.xlsx as a starting cadence and an automation script example.

Action items
- Dev (Dev Patel): provision sandbox service account + create sample token exchange flow and share creds for your infra team.
- Enterpriseco: send link to IdP admin & preferred OIDC audience claim.
- Marissa: set up deep-dive invite for Wed 6/21 10:00am PT.

Thanks —
Marissa

- Confirm which flows will use short-lived tokens vs scoped API keys
- Which models/endpoints to scope on the service account (inference, embeddings, reranker)

Deliverables by EOD today from Redwood: sandbox service account + initial token exchange sample (Python). I'll ping here when done.

Thanks all — wed 6/21 10:00am PT was great. Priya (infra) and our security engineer joined. Follow-ups from our side:
- We like the JWT exchange + OIDC approach. We will share IdP metadata and create a service account in our test tenant for the POC.
- Rotation cadence: security is comfortable with 30 days if automated; they asked for documentation on revocation on emergency compromise.
- Agreed to start with scoped service-account permissions: embeddings + rerankers + inference read-only.

Next steps (we accept):
1) Redwood to share sandbox service account + token exchange example (Dev) — ETA EOD 6/22
2) Enterpriseco to share IdP metadata + S3 export details — ETA EOD 6/23
3) Schedule follow-up integration test session next week to validate token exchange and logs.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the POC.

— Priya
